items.title: Bob Cranshaw interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: Joe Raposo was the first writer, was the musical director for the show and I fell into the job... from that time until his death, everything that Joe Raposo, all of his ventures... I was always involved.

ctx.x: We see the shirt right here.

Yeah. But I was 27 years with Sesame Street. It started out, I started to work, Joe Raposo was the first writer, was the musical director for the show and I fell into the job through Chuck Israels, another bass player who was in New York. And Chuck was doing an off- Broadway show called “House of Flowers.” And he was leaving, going to the state of Washington to teach at a university there. So he called me and asked me if I was interested in doing this off-Broadway show for him. He was leaving. So I said yeah I…

did. I knew, this I got from the Joe Williams kind of thing. And the Milt Hinton. If it feels good, I like things that really feel good. I can listen to a band play out of tune, but if it feels good, if they have a certain kind of energy, I’m attracted to it. And I was attracted to the Milt Hintons and the people like that because of the energy that I heard. The Oscar Peterson trio, I’m a big fan of Ray Brown. I’m a kind of Ray Brown clone. I like that excitement. I like that kind of energy. And I feel that’s the…
